# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**Member:** Cameron Carter
**Member ID:** W300143742
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-16
**Reference number:** POC-3469ABE4FC-29435
**Governing policy:** Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O) — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-ankle.pdf

Dear UnitedHealthcare / Oxford Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented is medically necessary. I am asking that this decision be reconsidered.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that this procedure "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," and points to the policy above. That same policy states:

> "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

The policy also states that the specific clinical criteria for this type of surgery are found elsewhere:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP:"

> "Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint) Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle Arthrotomy, Ankle Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

I have not been given the actual text of the InterQual criteria for "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle" that applies to my case. The denial notice does not quote or attach it. I want to be clear that the sections of the policy provided to me about osteochondral allograft and autograft transplant do not appear to describe my procedure — my surgery is a total ankle replacement, not a cartilage graft — so I do not believe those sections are the basis for comparing my records against the plan's own standard. Without the actual InterQual criteria that were applied to my request, I am not able to fully evaluate the reason for denial, and I do not believe it is possible to determine whether my records meet or fail to meet it.

**I am formally requesting, in writing, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination.** The policy itself states that UnitedHealthcare uses "tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits," and confirms that "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage." I am providing that documentation below, but I cannot respond to specific criteria that have not been shared with me. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to provide, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on in a denial, and I am asking for that now.

## My medical records

The following is what my surgeon's office has documented in support of this surgery:

- **Symptom duration:** 9 months of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Conservative care completed:** 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03), 24 visits, focused on ankle strengthening and balance, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** Corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-14, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** Weight-bearing ankle radiographs on 2026-06-28 showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.
- **Functional impact:** I walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks of walking.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, and range of motion limited by pain.
- **Other relevant history:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI of 29, non-smoker.

I believe this record reflects a sustained, well-documented course of conservative treatment that has not resolved my symptoms, along with imaging and exam findings that my surgeon has relied on in recommending this surgery.

## What I am asking for

1. Please provide, in writing, the specific InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text for "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle" that was applied to my request, as described above.
2. Please reconsider this denial in light of my complete medical record, which I understand my surgeon's office can also submit or has already submitted with the prior authorization request.
3. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and let me know if any additional information is needed.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-12. I am submitting it by signing in at member.uhc.com and filing it there, and I am also available at the number on my member ID card. I understand that the address printed on my denial letter is the authoritative one for submission, and I will use that address if it differs from the online portal.

Thank you for your time in reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

________________________________
Cameron Carter
Member ID: W300143742
Date: [insert date signed]
Contact phone/email: [insert contact information]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
